lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Trachea
lessons.subtitle: Respiratory epithelium, glands, perichondrium, and hyaline cartilage

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Orient from the luminal respiratory epithelium through lamina propria and pale seromucous glands to perichondrium and hyaline cartilage.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: The lining is ciliated pseudostratified columnar epithelium with goblet and basal cells.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Basal cells touch the basement membrane but do not reach the lumen; ciliated and goblet cells do.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: A broad outer cartilage band without surrounding lung parenchyma favors trachea; intrapulmonary bronchi have irregular plates within lung.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Orient from the luminal respiratory epithelium through lamina propria and pale seromucous glands to perichondrium and hyaline cartilage.
The lining is ciliated pseudostratified columnar epithelium with goblet and basal cells.
Basal cells touch the basement membrane but do not reach the lumen; ciliated and goblet cells do.
A broad outer cartilage band without surrounding lung parenchyma favors trachea; intrapulmonary bronchi have irregular plates within lung.

traps.wrong: Calling it bronchus because the lining is ciliated
traps.right: Use the complete wall sequence and context: gland-rich submucosa, broad cartilage, and no surrounding alveoli.

recognition: Respiratory epithelium, glands, perichondrium, and hyaline cartilage
A broad outer cartilage band without surrounding lung parenchyma favors trachea; intrapulmonary bronchi have irregular plates within lung.

source.label: Junqueira 16e + diFiore 11e
source.detail: Respiratory system / trachea; Junqueira Figure 17-5, PDF page 365.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Urinary bladder
lessons.subtitle: Folded urothelium over interlacing detrusor muscle

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Orient from the folded mucosa to a very thick wall of irregular smooth-muscle bundles.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Urothelium has small basal cells, intermediate cells, and large dome-shaped superficial umbrella cells.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Umbrella cells may be binucleate and flatten as the organ fills while preserving the urine barrier.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Bladder has a broad lumen and interlacing detrusor; ureter is smaller, often stellate, with more orderly muscle layers.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Orient from the folded mucosa to a very thick wall of irregular smooth-muscle bundles.
Urothelium has small basal cells, intermediate cells, and large dome-shaped superficial umbrella cells.
Umbrella cells may be binucleate and flatten as the organ fills while preserving the urine barrier.
Bladder has a broad lumen and interlacing detrusor; ureter is smaller, often stellate, with more orderly muscle layers.

traps.wrong: Counting a fixed number of urothelial layers
traps.right: Layer count and umbrella-cell shape vary with distension; identify the epithelial type and wall pattern.

recognition: Folded urothelium over interlacing detrusor muscle
Bladder has a broad lumen and interlacing detrusor; ureter is smaller, often stellate, with more orderly muscle layers.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Compact bone
lessons.subtitle: Osteons, lamellae, lacunae, and canaliculi

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Locate circular osteons built around central vascular Haversian canals.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Concentric lamellae contain osteocyte lacunae linked by fine radiating canaliculi.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Osteocytes occupy lacunae; osteoblasts line forming surfaces and osteoclasts are large multinucleated surface cells.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Mineralized concentric lamellae and central canals distinguish compact bone from avascular cartilage.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Locate circular osteons built around central vascular Haversian canals.
Concentric lamellae contain osteocyte lacunae linked by fine radiating canaliculi.
Osteocytes occupy lacunae; osteoblasts line forming surfaces and osteoclasts are large multinucleated surface cells.
Mineralized concentric lamellae and central canals distinguish compact bone from avascular cartilage.

traps.wrong: Calling every dark space a chondrocyte lacuna
traps.right: Look for concentric lamellae and canaliculi: those make it an osteon.

recognition: Osteons, lamellae, lacunae, and canaliculi
Mineralized concentric lamellae and central canals distinguish compact bone from avascular cartilage.

source.label: diFiore 11e + Junqueira 16e
source.detail: Compact bone osteon; diFiore Figure 4.19, PDF page 115.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Hyaline cartilage
lessons.subtitle: Glassy matrix, lacunae, and isogenous groups

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Look for an avascular glassy matrix bounded by perichondrium in most locations.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Rounded chondrocytes sit in lacunae, often as isogenous groups within darker territorial matrix.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Chondroblasts lie near the perichondrium; mature chondrocytes are deeper and enclosed in matrix.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Hyaline matrix hides its fine type II collagen; elastic cartilage shows elastic fibers and fibrocartilage shows thick type I bundles.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Look for an avascular glassy matrix bounded by perichondrium in most locations.
Rounded chondrocytes sit in lacunae, often as isogenous groups within darker territorial matrix.
Chondroblasts lie near the perichondrium; mature chondrocytes are deeper and enclosed in matrix.
Hyaline matrix hides its fine type II collagen; elastic cartilage shows elastic fibers and fibrocartilage shows thick type I bundles.

traps.wrong: Mistaking empty shrinkage spaces for the whole lacuna
traps.right: Identify the basophilic chondrocyte and its surrounding territorial matrix, not just the processing gap.

recognition: Glassy matrix, lacunae, and isogenous groups
Hyaline matrix hides its fine type II collagen; elastic cartilage shows elastic fibers and fibrocartilage shows thick type I bundles.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Synovial joint
lessons.subtitle: Articular cartilage, joint space, capsule, and synovium

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Find two opposing articular surfaces separated by a joint cavity and enclosed by a fibrous capsule.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Articular hyaline cartilage has zonal chondrocytes and no perichondrium; synovium lines non-articular internal surfaces.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Type A synoviocytes are macrophage-like; type B synoviocytes are fibroblast-like and produce matrix components.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: A true joint cavity plus opposing articular cartilage identifies a synovial joint.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Find two opposing articular surfaces separated by a joint cavity and enclosed by a fibrous capsule.
Articular hyaline cartilage has zonal chondrocytes and no perichondrium; synovium lines non-articular internal surfaces.
Type A synoviocytes are macrophage-like; type B synoviocytes are fibroblast-like and produce matrix components.
A true joint cavity plus opposing articular cartilage identifies a synovial joint.

traps.wrong: Calling the synovial lining an epithelium
traps.right: Synovium is specialized vascular connective tissue without a basement membrane or true epithelial sheet.

recognition: Articular cartilage, joint space, capsule, and synovium
A true joint cavity plus opposing articular cartilage identifies a synovial joint.

source.label: Junqueira 16e + Columbia Histology
source.detail: Joints and articular cartilage; course image cross-checked with academic virtual-lab descriptions.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Peripheral nerve
lessons.subtitle: Axons and Schwann cells organized into fascicles

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Identify round or oval fascicles enclosed by distinct perineurium within looser epineurial connective tissue.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Each axon is surrounded by endoneurium; dissolved myelin often leaves a pale ring around a central axon.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Schwann-cell nuclei are small and elongated; they myelinate one internode of one peripheral axon.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Perineurial fascicles distinguish nerve from tendon, which has parallel collagen without axons or myelin spaces.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Identify round or oval fascicles enclosed by distinct perineurium within looser epineurial connective tissue.
Each axon is surrounded by endoneurium; dissolved myelin often leaves a pale ring around a central axon.
Schwann-cell nuclei are small and elongated; they myelinate one internode of one peripheral axon.
Perineurial fascicles distinguish nerve from tendon, which has parallel collagen without axons or myelin spaces.

traps.right: Perineurium wraps one fascicle; epineurium binds multiple fascicles and larger vessels.

recognition: Axons and Schwann cells organized into fascicles
Perineurial fascicles distinguish nerve from tendon, which has parallel collagen without axons or myelin spaces.

source.label: diFiore 11e + Duke Histology
source.detail: Nervous tissue, peripheral nerve; diFiore Figure 7.15, PDF page 179.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Dorsal root ganglion
lessons.subtitle: Large sensory neurons ringed by satellite cells

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Look for a capsule, bundles of nerve fibers, and clusters of very large neuronal cell bodies.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Pseudounipolar sensory neurons have central nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and a nearly complete satellite-cell cuff.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Satellite glial cells form a tight ring around each neuronal soma and regulate its local microenvironment.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Orderly satellite-cell rings and central neuronal nuclei favor dorsal root ganglion over autonomic ganglion.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Look for a capsule, bundles of nerve fibers, and clusters of very large neuronal cell bodies.
Pseudounipolar sensory neurons have central nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and a nearly complete satellite-cell cuff.
Satellite glial cells form a tight ring around each neuronal soma and regulate its local microenvironment.
Orderly satellite-cell rings and central neuronal nuclei favor dorsal root ganglion over autonomic ganglion.

traps.wrong: Calling every small nucleus a lymphocyte
traps.right: Small nuclei directly cuffing a giant neuronal soma are satellite cells; Schwann cells follow axons.

recognition: Large sensory neurons ringed by satellite cells
Orderly satellite-cell rings and central neuronal nuclei favor dorsal root ganglion over autonomic ganglion.

source.label: diFiore 11e + SIU Histology
source.detail: Dorsal root ganglion; diFiore Figure 7.21, PDF page 185.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Thin skin with hair
lessons.subtitle: Hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and a thin epidermis

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Orient from a relatively thin epidermis into dermis containing oblique hair follicles and adnexal glands.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Sebaceous glands have pale foamy holocrine cells; arrector pili is a small smooth-muscle bundle attached to a follicle.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Hair-matrix keratinocytes proliferate around a dermal papilla; melanocytes transfer pigment to the forming hair.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Hair follicles and sebaceous glands identify thin hairy skin; thick glabrous skin lacks both.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Orient from a relatively thin epidermis into dermis containing oblique hair follicles and adnexal glands.
Sebaceous glands have pale foamy holocrine cells; arrector pili is a small smooth-muscle bundle attached to a follicle.
Hair-matrix keratinocytes proliferate around a dermal papilla; melanocytes transfer pigment to the forming hair.
Hair follicles and sebaceous glands identify thin hairy skin; thick glabrous skin lacks both.

traps.right: Confirm the adnexa: follicles plus sebaceous glands are decisive for skin with hair.

recognition: Hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and a thin epidermis
Hair follicles and sebaceous glands identify thin hairy skin; thick glabrous skin lacks both.

source.label: diFiore 11e + SIU Histology
source.detail: Integument, hairy skin; diFiore Figures 10.3–10.4, PDF page 241.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Thick skin without hair
lessons.subtitle: Very thick keratin, prominent ridges, and eccrine ducts

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Find an exceptionally thick stratum corneum with deep epidermal ridges and no pilosebaceous units.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: A pale stratum lucidum lies between the granular and cornified layers; coiled eccrine glands fill deep dermis and hypodermis.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Keratinocytes progress from basal mitotic cells through spinous, granular, lucid, and cornified compartments.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Hairless skin with a thick corneum and stratum lucidum is palm or sole; it lacks follicles and sebaceous glands.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Find an exceptionally thick stratum corneum with deep epidermal ridges and no pilosebaceous units.
A pale stratum lucidum lies between the granular and cornified layers; coiled eccrine glands fill deep dermis and hypodermis.
Keratinocytes progress from basal mitotic cells through spinous, granular, lucid, and cornified compartments.
Hairless skin with a thick corneum and stratum lucidum is palm or sole; it lacks follicles and sebaceous glands.

traps.wrong: Calling any hairless crop thick skin
traps.right: Require the full pattern: massive corneum, lucidum, deep ridges, and abundant eccrine structures.

recognition: Very thick keratin, prominent ridges, and eccrine ducts
Hairless skin with a thick corneum and stratum lucidum is palm or sole; it lacks follicles and sebaceous glands.

source.label: diFiore 11e + SIU Histology
source.detail: Integument, thick skin; diFiore Figure 10.7, PDF page 247.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: White adipose tissue
lessons.subtitle: Unilocular adipocytes with signet-ring profiles

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: The tissue resembles chicken wire because each large adipocyte lost one dominant lipid droplet during processing.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: A thin rim of cytoplasm and flattened peripheral nucleus surround the empty-appearing unilocular space.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: White adipocytes store triacylglycerol and secrete adipokines; delicate reticular fibers and capillaries support each cell.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: One large vacuole and an eccentric flattened nucleus distinguish white from multilocular brown adipocytes.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: The tissue resembles chicken wire because each large adipocyte lost one dominant lipid droplet during processing.
A thin rim of cytoplasm and flattened peripheral nucleus surround the empty-appearing unilocular space.
White adipocytes store triacylglycerol and secrete adipokines; delicate reticular fibers and capillaries support each cell.
One large vacuole and an eccentric flattened nucleus distinguish white from multilocular brown adipocytes.

traps.wrong: Calling the clear space an intracellular lumen
traps.right: It is the site of an extracted lipid droplet; the living cell is filled by lipid.

recognition: Unilocular adipocytes with signet-ring profiles
One large vacuole and an eccentric flattened nucleus distinguish white from multilocular brown adipocytes.

source.label: Junqueira 16e + SIU Histology
source.detail: Chapter 6, white adipose tissue; Figure 6-1, PDF page 134.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Brown adipose tissue
lessons.subtitle: Multilocular, mitochondria-rich thermogenic adipocytes

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Lobules contain smaller, darker cells and a very rich capillary network rather than large chicken-wire spaces.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Each brown adipocyte has many lipid droplets, a more central nucleus, and eosinophilic mitochondria-rich cytoplasm.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: UCP1 in the inner mitochondrial membrane uncouples oxidation from ATP synthesis to generate heat.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Multiple droplets and central nuclei distinguish brown adipocytes from unilocular white fat.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Lobules contain smaller, darker cells and a very rich capillary network rather than large chicken-wire spaces.
Each brown adipocyte has many lipid droplets, a more central nucleus, and eosinophilic mitochondria-rich cytoplasm.
UCP1 in the inner mitochondrial membrane uncouples oxidation from ATP synthesis to generate heat.
Multiple droplets and central nuclei distinguish brown adipocytes from unilocular white fat.

traps.wrong: Mistaking brown fat for an endocrine gland
traps.right: Confirm the many small lipid vacuoles in individual cells and the lobular vascular pattern.

recognition: Multilocular, mitochondria-rich thermogenic adipocytes
Multiple droplets and central nuclei distinguish brown adipocytes from unilocular white fat.

source.label: Junqueira 16e
source.detail: Chapter 6, brown adipose tissue; Figure 6-4a, PDF page 137.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Thyroid gland
lessons.subtitle: Colloid-filled follicles lined by simple epithelium

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: The gland is packed with round follicles of variable size, each filled by homogeneous eosinophilic colloid.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Follicular-cell height reflects activity: flatter in less-active follicles and cuboidal to columnar when stimulated.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Follicular cells produce T3 and T4; pale parafollicular C cells produce calcitonin and do not contact the follicular lumen.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Extracellular colloid within true follicles is unique among the common endocrine practical slides.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: The gland is packed with round follicles of variable size, each filled by homogeneous eosinophilic colloid.
Follicular-cell height reflects activity: flatter in less-active follicles and cuboidal to columnar when stimulated.
Follicular cells produce T3 and T4; pale parafollicular C cells produce calcitonin and do not contact the follicular lumen.
Extracellular colloid within true follicles is unique among the common endocrine practical slides.

traps.wrong: Calling colloid a lumen full of mucus
traps.right: Colloid is extracellular thyroglobulin; identify the complete follicular epithelial ring.

recognition: Colloid-filled follicles lined by simple epithelium
Extracellular colloid within true follicles is unique among the common endocrine practical slides.

source.label: Junqueira 16e + Yale MedCell
source.detail: Endocrine glands, thyroid; morphology cross-checked with an academic virtual slide.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Skeletal muscle
lessons.subtitle: Long striated fibers with multiple peripheral nuclei

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Parallel unbranched fascicles are separated by perimysium; individual fibers are wrapped by delicate endomysium.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Longitudinal fibers show cross-striations and multiple flattened nuclei immediately beneath the sarcolemma.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: A skeletal muscle fiber is one multinucleated syncytium; satellite cells lie outside its sarcolemma under the basal lamina.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Peripheral multiple nuclei and no branching distinguish skeletal from cardiac muscle.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Parallel unbranched fascicles are separated by perimysium; individual fibers are wrapped by delicate endomysium.
Longitudinal fibers show cross-striations and multiple flattened nuclei immediately beneath the sarcolemma.
A skeletal muscle fiber is one multinucleated syncytium; satellite cells lie outside its sarcolemma under the basal lamina.
Peripheral multiple nuclei and no branching distinguish skeletal from cardiac muscle.

traps.wrong: Calling a peripheral satellite-cell nucleus a myonucleus
traps.right: Myonuclei are inside the sarcolemma; satellite cells occupy a narrow external niche.

recognition: Long striated fibers with multiple peripheral nuclei
Peripheral multiple nuclei and no branching distinguish skeletal from cardiac muscle.

source.label: Junqueira 16e
source.detail: Chapter 10, skeletal muscle; Figure 10-1a, PDF page 205.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Cardiac muscle
lessons.subtitle: Branching striated myocytes joined by intercalated discs

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Myocytes form an irregular branching network with abundant endomysial capillaries rather than parallel fascicles.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Cells have one or two central nuclei, cross-striations, and dark transverse intercalated discs at cell boundaries.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Gap junctions electrically couple myocytes; fasciae adherentes and desmosomes transmit force and resist separation.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Branching cells, central nuclei, and intercalated discs distinguish cardiac from skeletal muscle.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Myocytes form an irregular branching network with abundant endomysial capillaries rather than parallel fascicles.
Cells have one or two central nuclei, cross-striations, and dark transverse intercalated discs at cell boundaries.
Gap junctions electrically couple myocytes; fasciae adherentes and desmosomes transmit force and resist separation.
Branching cells, central nuclei, and intercalated discs distinguish cardiac from skeletal muscle.

traps.wrong: Calling every transverse stripe an intercalated disc
traps.right: Discs are darker, less regularly spaced cell boundaries; sarcomeric striations repeat finely within each cell.

recognition: Branching striated myocytes joined by intercalated discs
Branching cells, central nuclei, and intercalated discs distinguish cardiac from skeletal muscle.

source.label: Junqueira 16e
source.detail: Chapter 10, cardiac muscle and intercalated discs.

lessons.subject: histology
lessons.title: Tendon
lessons.subtitle: Dense regular type I collagen with rows of tenocytes

visual.caption: Low power → high power → cell identity → closest discriminator

items.label: 1 · Orient
items.detail: Densely packed eosinophilic collagen runs in one direction with little ground substance or vascular space.
items.cue: Start at the edge and the lumen or capsule.

items.label: 2 · Zoom
items.detail: Sparse flattened tenocyte nuclei form dark rows squeezed between slightly wavy collagen bundles.
items.cue: Name the dominant architecture before a single cell.

items.label: 3 · Cells
items.detail: Tenocytes are specialized fibroblasts that maintain the parallel type I collagen matrix.
items.cue: Match nuclear position, cytoplasm, and matrix.

items.label: 4 · Separate
items.detail: Tendon lacks muscle striations and myofiber borders; unlike fibrocartilage, its cells do not sit in lacunae.
items.cue: Say why the closest look-alike loses.

essentials: Densely packed eosinophilic collagen runs in one direction with little ground substance or vascular space.
Sparse flattened tenocyte nuclei form dark rows squeezed between slightly wavy collagen bundles.
Tenocytes are specialized fibroblasts that maintain the parallel type I collagen matrix.
Tendon lacks muscle striations and myofiber borders; unlike fibrocartilage, its cells do not sit in lacunae.

traps.wrong: Mistaking longitudinal tendon for skeletal muscle
traps.right: Follow the nuclei: tendon nuclei are sparse, thin, and arranged between collagen bundles with no cross-striations.

recognition: Dense regular type I collagen with rows of tenocytes
Tendon lacks muscle striations and myofiber borders; unlike fibrocartilage, its cells do not sit in lacunae.

source.label: diFiore 11e
source.detail: Chapter 3, dense regular connective tissue; Figure 3.9, PDF page 85.
